methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $1.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
JetZero is a Series B-stage transportation company founded by Tom O'Leary and Mark Page. The company has raised over $1.0B to date. The relevant comp universe consists of 7 private firms in Transportation, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, and Parallel Systems. No public transportation comparables were available for direct valuation anchoring.

We applied stage-progression analysis as the primary valuation method. Using JetZero's $1.0B total raised as a proxy baseline and applying a typical Series B step-up multiplier of 1.9x yields an implied valuation of $1.9B. Peer-median analysis was not applicable; while 3 same-sector peers exist, insufficient overlap was found across same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier buckets to establish a reliable median benchmark (minimum 3 datapoints required per filter).

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.6B to $2.2B, with $1.9B as the point estimate. This range reflects ±15% variance around the stage-progression result, absent corroborating peer data. Key uncertainties include the timing and size of downstream capital rounds, which will materially affect realized valuation, and the lack of public or tightly comparable private benchmarks in the frontier-transportation segment to validate the 1.9x multiplier assumption.
